newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Pakistan airline needs 250,000/T jet fuel in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan airline needs 250,000/T jet fuel in 97/98.

text.p: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) would need to import 250,000 tonnes of jet fuel in 1997/1998, up from 225,000 tonnes it purchased in 1996/1997, a PIA source said on Friday.
PIA has requested for this volume from the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Resources for approval, he said. The higher volume is due to increased flight routes and frequencies.

The source said even though the volume would rise, PIA expects its budget for the new fiscal year (July 1-June 30) to be lower than the 7.9 billion rupees ($192.4 million) allotted for the current fiscal year.

An important reason for this is the lower average spot price of jet fuel in the Middle East which PIA is projecting in calculating its budget for 1997/1998 at $24.00 per barrel, compared with $27.00 in 1996/1997.

Trade sources said current MidEast spot price is around $23.00 per barrel free-on-board (fob) basis, while floating price is assessed at between parity and a 10-cent-per-barrel premium to MidEast spot quotes.
But traders noted that MidEast kerosene values should pick up to $24.00 sometime in August to peak during December-January as winter arrives.
Traders noted that average jet fuel price in Singapore, the Asian benchmark, from July last year to now was $28.80 per barrel, compared with $27.25 between July 1995-April 1996.

The PIA source said its import tender for the new fiscal year would likely be issued in June. The first delivery is expected to be made during late July/early August and not during early July which was the case in previous years.
This was because PIA would continue to take delivery of its last jet fuel cargoes for the current term contract in late June.
PIA has been buying term jet fuel from state-owned Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) since 1993 after Kuwait recovered from the 1990/1991 Gulf War.
The 1996/1997 contract was awarded at a premium of $1.45 per barrel to MidEast spot quotes, on a cost-insurance-freight (cif) basis to Karachi.
In 1995/1996, PIA bought 175,000 tonnes from KPC, at a $1.20-premium to MidEast spot quotes, cif basis.
